title: Studio-origin surfaces (reference selection, background keyframes, (+) tracks) through the REAL child→parent chain — re-diagnosis after 260921-e21 was falsified by native UAT
expected: The plan's FG table expected the drop at FG-1 (the guard returning null with dirty already cleared) or FG-2 (serializeRuntimeIntoDocument reverting the change on the way out) or FG-4 (a false close gate).
actual: FG-2 and FG-4 are GREEN for these three surfaces (measured) and FG-1 is GREEN for a simple composition — the e21 trap, again. The drop is at the SAME composite link FG-1 names, one level deeper: the failure-path re-arm e21 added is NOT REACHABLE from the retry that follows it. MEASURED, all three surfaces: rearmWroteTheRefNotTheCapturedConst=true; the retry against the render-captured const returnsNull=true with emitCount=0 and owedAfterRetry=false; the identical retry against the re-armed ref returnsNull=false with emitCount=1 (the control).
note: All probe output below is raw and verbatim from the run at this head. Nothing is summarised from a probe that was not run.

FG-1.whatTheGapWas: e21 handed the document straight to sendEfxPaintDocumentSync and pinned the guard with a SOURCE-TEXT assertion, so the guard-in-the-loop behaviour (a null return consuming a cleared dirty flag) was never entered.
FG-1.howThisRunClosedIt: Every push-shaped probe routes its document through createDocumentSyncPushGuard().evaluate(() => serializeRuntimeIntoDocument(layerId), () => efxPaintVersion.peek()) exactly as pushLiveProjection does (:3922-3931), and the caller contract (dirty cleared BEFORE the call) is driven with a signal, not asserted from source text.
FG-1.observedControlResult: FIRST evaluate non-null (a real send) and the SECOND, re-entrant evaluate on the same guard returns null with dirtyAfterClear=false and documentStillOwed=false — the drop SHAPE is real and measured, but on a duplicate where nothing is lost. The reachable drop is step 8: after a FAILED send, the re-arm writes the ref while the decision reads the render-captured const, so the retry returns null with nothing owed.

FG-2.whatTheGapWas: e21 used a HAND-BUILT document, or serialized in the realm that had not mutated.
FG-2.howThisRunClosedIt: d1 = revision of the child document BEFORE serialize, d2 = the revision of the document serialize RETURNED, d3 = the revision of the child document AFTER the write-back (efxPaintStore.ts:1708-1734).
FG-2.observedControlResult: GREEN — serializeThrew=null, d2 === d3 (efxdoc-659-5ee832d9), documentRevision 4 -> 5, returnedIsStoredObject=true, and all three surfaces carried before AND after. FG-2 is EXONERATED for these three surfaces: the write-back does not revert them.

FG-3.whatTheGapWas: e21 drove ONE module instance and faked the parent realm with resetEfxPaintStore() mid-test, so module-level state (documents, runtimes, documentSyncSentDigests) leaked across the 'boundary'.
FG-3.howThisRunClosedIt: TWO real module instances: the child realm imported first, then vi.resetModules(), then the parent realm (efxPaintStore, physicPaintStore, transport, guard, document module, revision module). The realm control is asserted before any probe.
FG-3.observedControlResult: PASS — separateInstances=true, separateEfxVersionSignals=true, separatePhysicStores=true, childDocumentVisibleInChild=true, childDocumentVisibleInParent=false (a child-only document is INVISIBLE to the parent until the send crosses).

FG-4.whatTheGapWas: e21 never drove the close sequence at all.
FG-4.howThisRunClosedIt: The close gate (:1919) is composed with the real terms, evaluated for the state EACH surface's mutation leaves (dirty=true, failures=0), then the flush body (:4013-4027) is driven through the mode gate and the clear, and the resulting push's outcome is recorded.
FG-4.observedControlResult: GREEN for the gate itself — for each of the three surfaces the gate WOULD fire (true), the flush WOULD clear inside the mode gate and WOULD push. The push it then makes is the step-8 link: against a failed send's stale const it returns null, the flush reports a clean outcome, and the close sequence destroys the window with the parent stale.

step7_strokesContrast.theSentence: A stroke survives teardown because it never rides this channel: it is emitted eagerly on physic-paint:apply, answered by physic-paint:apply-result, and needs no dirty flag, no guard, no debounce and no close flush. These three surfaces ride physic-paint:efx-paint-document, which has NO ack — so the child cannot tell a delivered push from a consumed one, and the single failure path that could re-send (the :3981 re-arm) is unreachable from the retry that follows it while the caller has already cleared the flag that would have kept the change owed.

step8_rearmReachability.note: A failed push arms a retry the component cannot reach: the re-arm writes the ref (:3981) while the decision reads the render-captured const (:3913/:3922). The retry then sees the failed content as a duplicate and consumes it — no send, no re-mark.
step8_rearmReachability.modelledWindow: no re-render between the failure and the retry. In the product this window is real for the CLOSE push: the render the push's own serialize schedules happens BEFORE the rejection lands (the rejection needs the await chain through projectEfxPaintDocumentForSync + the dynamic import), and the .catch's own re-mark (:3984) is a no-op because the serialize already set the flag — so nothing guarantees a render after the write.
